title: ApplyOps
description: INPUT of `dmtool -m <model> apply <ops.json>` (CLI-SPEC §7) — an ORDERED array of op-records applied to ONE model in a single session: one read → ordered surgery → one terminal kernel gate → one write, with atomic rollback (a mid-sequence failure writes nothing). Each op-record is {target, op, …args}; the per-op fields are that verb's params — discover them from `manifest` + `schema <target> <op>`. The locator key for an EXISTING element matches the standalone verb's positional: a path-located element uses `<element>PathInModel`, a typedef `typeDefId`, an include `alias`; the polymorphic metadata operation is `{target:"meta",op:"modify",ref,…}` because `ref` accepts an element name-path or typedef id. `meta modify` is the sole post-creation common-metadata write route; field/group/rule modify records keep only their semantic properties. Rule and field add may still carry creation metadata. A REPEATABLE key takes a JSON array in an op-record, but a bare scalar also binds as one item. The op-set spans add·modify·remove·read plus the reference-rewriting refactors. A refused op or terminal kernel rejection rolls the whole sequence back. Distinct from `batch` (which takes {verb,args} for stateless per-op dispatch). Each edit result is `staged`/`written:false` until the wrapper commits; the wrapper's committed/written/summary fields are authoritative.

target.description: the element family acted on: field | group | rule | … (see `manifest`)

op.description: the operation: add | modify | remove | read | rename | move (valid for the target; see `manifest`)

time-zone.description: for config modify: absence defaults UTC; exact UTC, GMT, Europe/Berlin are interpreter-supported; another kernel-valid Java id is accepted with an evaluator-scope warning; blank/unknown ids are rejected

supported-character.description: for config modify: one singleton BMP character, inclusive x-y range, or atomic combined grapheme per entry; an empty/absent model list selects the full BMP excluding surrogates (not supplementary-plane characters)

metaModify.title: meta-modify-op
metaModify.description: Value-shape contract for `{target:"meta",op:"modify",ref,…}`. Map-valued directives are objects; repeatable removal directives accept the apply-wide scalar-or-array convention.
